sections.title: Data contracts (the octane/data check, not Strong mode)

diagnostics.detects: Effect setup calls a state updater synchronously. This includes updaters and callbacks returned by same-module custom hooks, and callbacks that run before the next paint: `startTransition`, a `useTransition` start function, `queueMicrotask`, `.then`/`.catch`/`.finally` on `Promise.resolve(value)` or `Promise.reject()`, `setTimeout` without a positive delay, and code after an `await` that resumes without waiting on any path, such as `await null` or `await (flag ? load() : null)`.
diagnostics.replacement: Derive the value during render, or use `useLinkedState` when state follows another value. When the effect copies a measurement of the committed DOM into state, render from `useLayoutSnapshot` instead. `requestAnimationFrame`, timers with a positive delay, and external subscription callbacks remain event-driven.

diagnostics.detects: A host element's callback ref calls a state updater synchronously: an inline or local function, a state setter passed as the ref, or a function in a `ref={[...]}` list. Octane calls a callback ref while the element commits, before paint, so it follows the effect setup rules, and callbacks that run before the next paint, such as `startTransition`, `queueMicrotask`, and `setTimeout` without a positive delay, count too. A component's `ref` prop is not checked, because the component decides when to call it.
diagnostics.replacement: Pass a ref object to keep the element, and read it from effects and event handlers. When the callback copies a measurement of the element into state, render from `useLayoutSnapshot` instead. `requestAnimationFrame`, timers with a positive delay, and observer or listener callbacks the ref attaches remain event-driven.

diagnostics.detects: A state update runs after an `await`, or in a `.then`, `.catch`, or `.finally` callback, of work the effect started, and the returned cleanup does not provably cancel or ignore it. An async effect callback returns a promise, so it cannot return cleanup.
diagnostics.replacement: Read asynchronous render data with `use()` or a query binding. For external synchronization, abort an `AbortController` whose `signal` is passed to the request, or set a flag declared in the effect from its cleanup and check it before the update.

diagnostics.detects: Synchronous effect setup reads a reassigned module `let` or `var`. It is not an inferred dependency, so the effect does not re-run when it changes, and every instance shares it. Calling a state getter and reading or writing a ref's `current` in an effect stay legal; neither is a dependency.
diagnostics.replacement: Keep the value in state, a prop, or context and read its snapshot, or move the non-reactive read into a `useEffectEvent` callback. Octane never double-invokes effects, so `didInit` guards are unnecessary.

diagnostics.detects: Effect setup acquires a platform listener, timer, observer, connection, or geolocation watch that the returned cleanup does not release. A `useLayoutSnapshot` measurement is checked like effect setup, but its return value is the snapshot, so it can never release one.
diagnostics.replacement: Release it in the returned cleanup. Acquire resources for a snapshot in a separate effect.

diagnostics.detects: A `useLayoutSnapshot` measurement is an `async` or generator function. It returns a new promise or iterator on every commit, so the snapshot never converges.
diagnostics.replacement: Return the measurement synchronously, and read asynchronous render data with `use()` or a query binding.

diagnostics.detects: A `useLayoutSnapshot` measurement writes to an element the template renders: its style, class, attributes, children, or scroll offset. Octane runs the queued measurements together so the browser lays out once, and a write between them makes every later read lay out again.
diagnostics.replacement: Return the measurement only. Render the value from the snapshot, or move the write to `useLayoutEffect`.

diagnostics.detects: A function writes to an element the template renders (its style, class, attributes, children, or scroll offset) and then reads its layout, such as `offsetHeight` or `getBoundingClientRect()`, before the browser has laid out. The read makes the browser lay out synchronously. In a loop that does both, every pass lays out again. A read whose value is dropped, such as `void element.offsetHeight`, is a deliberate flush and is not reported.
diagnostics.replacement: Read first, then write. In a loop, read every value in one pass and write in a second. Leave the read where it is when the value depends on the write.

diagnostics.detects: An effect reads state written by another effect's own execution or promise continuation in the same component.
diagnostics.replacement: Derive the value during render, use `useLinkedState`, or combine the external synchronization in one effect. External subscription and timer callbacks remain event-driven updates.

diagnostics.detects: An eager `useState` initializer or two-argument `useReducer` initial state is derived from component props.
diagnostics.replacement: Use `useLinkedState(source, reconcile)` for state that follows a source. Use `useState(() => initialValue)` or an explicit third `useReducer` initializer for a deliberate initial capture.

diagnostics.detects: An effect or imperative handle dependency argument differs from the compiler's inferred inputs, or cannot be proven equivalent. An array the compiler proves equivalent is reported as a **hint** instead, and its authored behavior is preserved.
diagnostics.replacement: Omit the dependency argument.

diagnostics.detects: An effect or imperative handle receives `null` dependencies, or omits them while its callback reads a binding declared after the hook, or a variable the component assigns after the hook or from a nested function. Inference cannot read that value where the hook is called, so the hook would run on every render.
diagnostics.replacement: Omit the argument so the compiler tracks reactive inputs. Declare and finish assigning what the hook reads before calling it, or keep a changing value in state or a ref.

diagnostics.detects: A statically known Effect Event is listed in an explicit hook dependency array.
diagnostics.replacement: Remove it. Effect Events are non-reactive, so they never belong in dependencies.

diagnostics.detects: A module compiled through the `manualSlots` integration option has a declaration Strong compilation would cache. That option cannot allocate the extra hook slots the cache needs.
diagnostics.replacement: Compile the module through the normal Octane integration, or keep it in compatibility mode.

diagnostics.detects: A `useState` or `useLinkedState` updater, a `useReducer` reducer, or a `useOptimistic` reducer calls `fetch`, schedules a timer, microtask, or promise callback, updates state, calls a state getter or Effect Event, reads or writes `useRef.current`, reads a browser global or reassigned module variable, or calls `Date.now()`, `Math.random()`, `performance.now()`, or `new Date()`. Octane can run updaters and reducers more than once.
diagnostics.replacement: Do the side effect or nondeterministic read in the event handler, effect, or Action, and pass its result in: `const now = Date.now(); setValue((current) => current + now)`.

diagnostics.detects: A state value is mutated outside render: in an event handler, effect, cleanup, deferred callback, or an updater or reducer's own state argument. Covers assignments, updates, `delete`, destructuring targets, `Object.assign` and `Reflect.set`-style targets, array mutators on state initialized with an array literal, and `Map`/`Set` mutators on state created with `new Map()` or `new Set()`.
diagnostics.replacement: Pass a new value, for example `setItems([...items, item])` or `setItems((current) => [...current, item])`. Keep mutable objects in `useRef`, or create one with `useLazyRef`.

diagnostics.detects: After an `await`, or in a timer or promise callback, a setter or dispatch argument reads the render snapshot of the same state, including through a local computed from it, a copied alias, or a closure.
diagnostics.replacement: Use the updater form, `setValue((current) => current + 1)`, compute from the state a reducer receives, or read the latest value with the state getter (the third tuple member).

diagnostics.detects: A function calls a state setter or reducer dispatch as a statement, then reads that state later in the same block or a nested one, for example `setDraft(""); if (draft) send(draft)` or `setCount(count + 1); log(count)`. The read sees the render snapshot, not the value just set. Reads in the setter argument, in updater functions, in nested functions, through the state getter, through a parameter or local alias, and in a sibling branch are not reported.
diagnostics.replacement: Compute the next value once and use it for both: `const next = count + 1; setCount(next); log(next)`. When the old value is what you mean, name it first: `const previous = count; setCount(0); log(previous)`.

diagnostics.detects: A declaration takes the value from a `useState` call and discards its setter, for example `const [value] = useState(initial)` or `const value = useState(initial)[0]`. This includes lazy initializers.
diagnostics.replacement: Derive render values from their inputs. Use `useInitialValue(value)` for a deliberate initial render snapshot. Pass a factory to initialize lazily. Use `useRef(value)` or `useLazyRef(() => createValue())` for mutable values kept for events or effects.

diagnostics.detects: A state tuple whose value is elided, unused, or read only to compute its own next value, whose getter is absent or unused, and whose setter is used. This is the force-update pattern, including `useReducer((x) => x + 1, 0)` and `useState(0)[1]`.
diagnostics.replacement: Subscribe with `useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, getSnapshot, getServerSnapshot)` and render its snapshot, or remove the unused state.

diagnostics.detects: Every return of a `useSyncExternalStore` `getSnapshot` or `getServerSnapshot` provably allocates: an object or array literal, `.map()`, `.filter()`, or another array copy, `Object.keys()`-style results, a standard constructor, or a same-module function or local constant that does so.
diagnostics.replacement: Return a value the store keeps, such as its current state object, or read each field with its own `useSyncExternalStore` call.

diagnostics.detects: A `useState`, `useReducer`, or `useLinkedState` updater is called during render, including inside callbacks that known array methods run synchronously.
diagnostics.replacement: Update state in an event handler, or use `useLinkedState` when state needs to reset or change with another value.

diagnostics.detects: A known third-tuple state getter is called during render. It can return scheduled state that differs from the render snapshot.
diagnostics.replacement: Render from the first tuple member. Call the getter in an event, effect, or deferred callback for the latest scheduled state.

diagnostics.detects: A `useRef` or `useLazyRef` object's `current` is read during render, including React's lazy initialization test `if (ref.current === null)`.
diagnostics.replacement: Read the ref in an event or effect, or render from state or `useLinkedState`. Create a value once with `useLazyRef(() => value)`, and render from a DOM measurement with `useLayoutSnapshot`. Pass the ref itself to a `ref` prop as usual.

diagnostics.detects: A `useRef` object's `current` is assigned during render, including React's lazy initialization `ref.current = create()` and `ref.current ??= create()`, and the latest-value pattern `latest.current = value`.
diagnostics.replacement: Create a value once with `useLazyRef(() => create())`. Read the latest props or state from an effect with `useEffectEvent`. Otherwise move the write to an event or effect, or express the value as state. `octane analyze --fix` rewrites the lazy initialization idiom.

diagnostics.detects: A reassigned module-scope `let` or `var` is read during render. It can change without a witnessed render input.
diagnostics.replacement: Move the changing value into state or context, or pass an immutable snapshot as a prop.

diagnostics.detects: Unshadowed `window`, `document`, `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, `navigator`, `location`, or `matchMedia` is read during render, including `typeof` guards and constant browser handle aliases, and `globalThis` properties other than standard language builtins.
diagnostics.replacement: Subscribe with `useSyncExternalStore` and a server snapshot for live browser state. Read a one-time value in an effect or a lazy `useState` initializer; lazy initializers also run during server rendering, so guard browser APIs there and keep server and client output the same.

diagnostics.detects: A provable state snapshot is mutated during render.
diagnostics.replacement: Derive a local copy, or pass a new value to the state updater from an event.

diagnostics.detects: A retained keyed `@for` row mutates a binding declared outside that row. A retained row does not re-run when its item is unchanged.
diagnostics.replacement: Build mutable data before the `@for`, or derive each row only from its item. Fresh setup-local and row-local scratch data remain valid.

diagnostics.detects: Unshadowed `Date.now()`, `Math.random()`, `performance.now()`, `Date()`, `new Date()`, `crypto.randomUUID()`, or `crypto.getRandomValues()` during render, including inside callbacks that known array methods run synchronously. A `key` or `@for` key built from one of these gets its own message.
diagnostics.replacement: Read time or randomness in an event handler or effect and store the result in state, or pass it in as a prop. Use `useId()` for element IDs. Give each list item a stable ID from its data, such as `item.id`.

diagnostics.detects: During render, `toLocaleString()`, `toLocaleDateString()`, or `toLocaleTimeString()` on a provable `Date` without both a locale and a visible `timeZone` option; `toString()` or `toTimeString()` on a provable `Date`; an `Intl` service constructed without a locale (a `DateTimeFormat` also needs a `timeZone`); or a call on a module-level formatter created that way.
diagnostics.replacement: Pass an explicit locale and time zone, for example `toLocaleString('en-US', { timeZone: 'UTC' })` or `new Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, { timeZone })`. Otherwise format in an event or effect and render the stored text.

diagnostics.detects: Unshadowed `setTimeout()`, `setInterval()`, `queueMicrotask()`, `requestAnimationFrame()`, or `requestIdleCallback()` during render, directly, on `window` or `globalThis`, or through an unreassigned alias. Lazy state and ref initializers are part of render for this check.
diagnostics.replacement: Schedule the work from an event handler, or from an effect that cancels it in cleanup. Defining a callback that schedules later stays valid; calling it during render does not.

diagnostics.detects: A statically known `useEffectEvent` result is called during render.
diagnostics.replacement: Call it from an effect, or from a later event or subscription callback.

diagnostics.detects: In `.tsrx`, a `.map()` callback returns JSX, including known local callback aliases.
diagnostics.replacement: Use `@for` with a stable item key. Data-only mapping remains valid.

diagnostics.detects: An `@for` key uses the loop position as its identity, including arithmetic or text derived from the index.
diagnostics.replacement: Use an item ID that survives insertion, removal, and reordering. Looking up an item ID, such as `items[index].id`, remains valid.

diagnostics.detects: An `@for` iterates a one-item array literal, such as `@for (const item of [value]; key item)`, or a `const` holding one that nothing but `@for` headers reads. A one-row loop is a workaround for a keyed remount or a local binding.
diagnostics.replacement: To remount a subtree when a value changes, wrap it in `<Fragment key={value}>…</Fragment>` or put `key` on its only element or component. To render one value, render it directly. Literals with two or more items and spreads stay valid.

diagnostics.detects: In `.tsrx`, a built-in hook value, or an effect that depends on it, is declared outside the sole nested `@{…}` block that uses it.
diagnostics.replacement: Move the hook into that block, before the JSX or local effect that uses its value. Hooks used only by conditional, keyed, switch, or try arms may stay in the parent scope to keep that lifetime.

diagnostics.detects: In `.tsrx`, a named native event handler is declared outside the sole deeper nested `@{…}` block that contains its direct `onX` use.
diagnostics.replacement: Move the handler into that block, before the JSX that uses it, or inline it.

diagnostics.detects: `"use strong"` appears somewhere other than the module's directive prologue, such as inside a function or after an import. It applies to a whole module, so the misplaced directive enables nothing.
diagnostics.replacement: Move `"use strong"` to the top of the file, before imports or other code.

diagnostics.detects: A `.tsx` or `.jsx` module is Strong, through its own `"use strong"` directive or the application's `compiler.strong` setting. Its JSX lowers to element descriptors, which render through the generic descriptor renderer instead of compiled templates. Installed dependencies keep their own mode.
diagnostics.replacement: Rename the module to `.tsrx` and write its markup as template JSX, with `@if`, `@for`, `@switch`, and `@try` blocks for control flow. A module without JSX can be `.ts` or `.js`; `root.render(App, props)` renders an entry point without JSX.

diagnostics.detects: A DOM intrinsic uses `suppressHydrationWarning` or `suppressNativeChangeWarning`, including statically visible object spreads.
diagnostics.replacement: Fix the mismatch or use the intended native event. Component props with these names are unaffected.

diagnostics.detects: A native text `onChange` handler, which fires on blur rather than per edit. The compatibility-mode warning is an error in Strong mode.
diagnostics.replacement: Use `onInput` for per-edit changes. Native checkbox, radio, and select `onChange` semantics stay valid.

diagnostics.detects: Imports or known namespace accesses for `flushSync`, `unstable_batchedUpdates`, or `StrictMode` from `octane`.
diagnostics.replacement: Use normal Octane scheduling and component semantics.

diagnostics.detects: Imports or known namespace accesses for `createElement`, `cloneElement`, `isValidElement`, `Children`, or `descriptorChildren` from `octane`, or for `jsx`, `jsxs`, `jsxDEV`, or `Fragment` from an Octane JSX runtime entry. The module creates or inspects element descriptors, which render through the generic descriptor renderer instead of compiled templates.
diagnostics.replacement: Write template JSX, pass the component itself (`icon={Plus}`), or pass a `() => @{ … }` render function. Type-only imports such as `ElementDescriptor` stay valid.

diagnostics.detects: A write through a ref to what the template owns on its element: its children, its class, an attribute it sets, or a `style` property it sets.
diagnostics.replacement: Render the value from state or props in the template.

diagnostics.detects: `innerHTML`, `outerHTML`, `insertAdjacentHTML()`, or `setHTMLUnsafe()` on an element Octane renders.
diagnostics.replacement: Use `dangerouslySetInnerHTML={trustHTML(html)}` for trusted or already sanitized HTML.

diagnostics.detects: `document.getElementById()`, `querySelector()`, `querySelectorAll()`, or `getElementsByClassName()` with a literal selector that matches a literal `id` or class rendered by the same component.
diagnostics.replacement: Attach a ref to the element and use `ref.current` in the event or effect.

diagnostics.detects: An event handler on a rendered element reads its event's `currentTarget` after it has returned: after an `await`, or in a timer or promise callback. `currentTarget` names the element only while the event is dispatched, so the read is empty.
diagnostics.replacement: Capture the element with `const element = event.currentTarget` at the top of the handler and use `element` afterwards.

diagnostics.detects: A visibly raw value is passed to a Strong DOM intrinsic's `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`.
diagnostics.replacement: Pass `trustHTML(html)` after applying the application's sanitization policy. `trustHTML` marks trust and does not sanitize.

diagnostics.detects: `octane analyze` with an `octane-strong-baseline.json`: a module compiles without Strong mode and is not listed. It is new, or it lost its directive or moved out of `compiler.strong`'s reach.
diagnostics.replacement: Add `"use strong"` before its imports, or enable `compiler.strong`, and fix what Strong then reports.

diagnostics.detects: A module listed in `octane-strong-baseline.json` is now Strong, no longer exists, or is no longer compiled by Octane. A stale name would let that module leave Strong mode again unnoticed.
diagnostics.replacement: Run `octane analyze --strong-baseline update`.

diagnostics.detects: With `compiler.strongDependencies.require`, an application import reaches a module in another Octane package that compiles without Strong mode, directly, through re-exports, or behind that package's own Strong modules, or it reaches an `octane/react` (ReactCompat) boundary. The build fails at the import, and `octane analyze` reports the same error.
diagnostics.replacement: Make the package Strong and declare it with `"octane": { "strong": true }` or a list of its Strong paths in its package.json, or name the package (or `"octane/react"`) in `compiler.strongDependencies.allow`.

diagnostics.detects: A call to `entity`, `read`, `view`, `write`, or `feed` from `octane/data` is not the whole initializer of an exported module-level `const`, its `name` (or an entity's first argument) is not a string literal, its options object spreads another object, or two contracts in the module share a name. The build cannot list a contract it cannot read without running the module.
diagnostics.replacement: Declare each contract as `export const setRead = write({ name: 'books.setRead', … })` in a `*.data.ts` module. Instead of building contracts in a function, declare one contract whose `input` carries the value.

diagnostics.detects: A contract is declared in a module whose file name does not end in `.data.ts` or `.data.js`, or a contract module has a top-level statement other than an import, a type, or a `const` declaration or export, or imports `octane/server` or `octane/data/server`. The browser and the server both import a contract module, so it must stay inert.
diagnostics.replacement: Move the contracts into a `*.data.ts` module, and move statements that run for effect, and server imports, into a module that imports the contracts.

diagnostics.detects: A contract site, such as `store.write`, `store.read`, `useForm`, `useWrite`, `handle`, `pages`, `listen`, `view({ of })`, or a feed change's `put`, receives a contract chosen at runtime: a conditional, a logical expression, or a computed member such as `contracts[name]`. Sites are matched by method, import, or property name, never by the receiver.
diagnostics.replacement: Name one contract binding at the site, such as `store.write(setRead, input)`, and pass the varying value in its input. A handler for several contracts may loop over an inline array of them: `[books, unread].map((list) => handle(list, …))`.

diagnostics.detects: A contract binding is used somewhere other than a contract site, an inline array a site loops over, an import or export, a type, or the object of a property read: for example passed to an app helper, stored in a variable, array, or map, or passed as a prop. The build could no longer find every use of the contract.
diagnostics.replacement: Pass a callback that names the contract, such as `submit(session, (store) => store.write(setRead, input))`, or move code that must take any contract into a module outside the check.

recipes.title: Capture an initial render value
recipes.note: The factory captures the initial value for this mount. Use a derived value when it should follow later inputs.

recipes.title: Use the value you just set
recipes.strong: const message = draft; setDraft(''); if (message) send(message);
recipes.note: A setter schedules a re-render; it does not change the value this render captured. Naming the value once makes clear which one each read means, and it stays correct if the code is reordered.

recipes.title: Create a value once
recipes.note: `useLazyRef` runs its factory once, when the hook cell is created, and keeps the ref on later renders. The factory follows the rules of a lazy `useState` initializer. `octane analyze --fix` applies this rewrite when the `useRef` declaration directly precedes the `if`.

recipes.title: Render from a DOM measurement
recipes.note: `useLayoutSnapshot` measures after each commit and re-renders before paint only when the value changes. `initial` is the value for the first render and for server rendering. It does not observe later resizes: subscribe to those with an observer in an effect.

recipes.title: Measure an element from a callback ref
recipes.note: A callback ref runs while the element commits, so a state update there renders the component a second time before paint. `useLayoutSnapshot` reads the element after layout on every commit and re-renders only when the measurement changes. To follow resizes that happen without a commit, attach a `ResizeObserver` from the ref or an effect; its callback may update state.

recipes.title: Read the latest props from an effect
recipes.note: An Effect Event always calls the latest `onTick` without making the effect depend on it.

recipes.title: Keep editable state in sync with a prop
recipes.note: `useLinkedState` resets the editable value in the same render whenever its source changes, so there is no frame with the stale value.

recipes.title: Render live browser state
recipes.note: The server snapshot is rendered on the server and during hydration, so both agree.

recipes.title: Generate an element ID
recipes.note: `useId` is stable across renders and matches between server and client.

recipes.title: Load data in an effect
recipes.strong: let ignore = false; load(id).then((p) => { if (!ignore) setName(p.name); }); return () => { ignore = true; };
recipes.note: Without the flag, a slow response for an old `id` can overwrite a newer one. For data the render needs, `use()` or a query binding avoids the effect entirely.

recipes.title: Re-render when an external store changes
recipes.note: `useSyncExternalStore` re-checks the snapshot after commit, so a change between render and subscription is not lost.

recipes.title: Render trusted HTML
recipes.note: `trustHTML` marks the value as trusted; it does not sanitize. Call it only on sanitized or already trusted HTML.
